title: Derived Hom from a nonpositive complex into a module
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site small in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and derived internal Hom computed by a K-injective resolution in the second argument [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Let $E\in D(\mathcal O)$ satisfy $\mathcal H^i(E)=0$ for $i>0$, and let $M$ be an $\mathcal O$-module, placed in degree zero. Then $\mathcal H^i(R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(E,M[0]))=0$ for every $i<0$. The canonical truncation map $E\to\mathcal H^0(E)[0]$ induces a bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal H^0(E),M)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O)}(E,M[0]),$$
where an ordinary module map is first viewed as a map of single complexes and then precomposed with truncation. This bijection is natural in $E$ and $M$. Here $\mathcal H^i$ is the cohomology sheaf of a representative, and no bounded-below, perfectness, quasi-coherence, Noetherian or enough-projectives hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Choose a complex $C$ representing $E$ and put $P=\tau_{\le0}C$, with its canonical inclusion $e:P\to C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-cohomology], $H^i(e)$ is an isomorphism for $i\le0$ and $H^i(P)=0$ for $i>0$. The hypothesis on $E$ therefore makes $e$ a quasi-isomorphism. Thus $QP\cong E$, $P^p=0$ for $p>0$, and $H^0(P)\cong\mathcal H^0(E)$; here $P^0=\ker d_C^0$ and $H^0(P)=\operatorname{coker}(d_P^{-1}:P^{-1}\to P^0)$.

source.place: Tag 0118 (section-truncations), canonical upper truncation; derived.tex Tag 06XS (lemma-negative-exts), first truncation in the proof

proof.text: The smallness assumption permits application of the Grothendieck-abelian assertion in [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] to $\Mod(\mathcal O)$. By [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] it has enough injectives. Apply part (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero] to choose $s:M[0]\to I$ with $I^q=0$ for $q<0$, all $I^q$ injective, and $0\to M\xrightarrow{s^0}I^0\xrightarrow{d_I^0}I^1\to\cdots$ exact. By [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective], $I$ is K-injective. In particular $s^0$ identifies $M$ with $\ker d_I^0$.

By [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], the representatives $P$ and $I$ compute $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(E,M[0])$ by $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,I)$. For $n<0$ its degree-$n$ term is $\prod_p\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(P^p,I^{p+n})$ by [def-pur-hom-complex]. If $p>0$ then $P^p=0$; if $p\le0$ then $p+n<0$ and $I^{p+n}=0$. Each factor is therefore the zero sheaf: over every localized site the only map from or to the zero module is zero. The whole product is zero. Consequently this representing complex is zero in every negative degree, so its negative cohomology sheaves vanish by the kernel/image definition of cohomology.

source.place: Section 08J7 (section-internal-hom), K-injective representative construction; Section 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), product formula

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] to $P$ and $I$: localization is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal O)}(P,I)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O)}(QP,QI)$. Composing with the isomorphisms $Qe:QP\to E$ and $Qs:M[0]\to QI$ gives a bijection from homotopy classes of chain maps $P\to I$ to $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O)}(E,M[0])$, sending $[f]$ to $(Qs)^{-1}\circ Qf\circ(Qe)^{-1}$. No boundedness of $P$ below is needed in the cited statement.

A chain map $f:P\to I$ has only the component $f^0:P^0\to I^0$: for $p<0$ its target is zero, and for $p>0$ its source is zero. Its two possibly nontrivial chain conditions are $d_I^0f^0=0$ and $f^0d_P^{-1}=0$. Since $M\xrightarrow{s^0}\ker d_I^0$ is an isomorphism, the first condition uniquely writes $f^0=s^0g$; since $s^0$ is monic, the second says $gd_P^{-1}=0$. The cokernel property uniquely writes $g=u\pi$ with $u:H^0(P)\to M$ and $\pi:P^0\twoheadrightarrow H^0(P)$. Conversely these formulas construct a chain map for every $u$. A chain homotopy has components $h^p:P^p\to I^{p-1}$; for $p\le0$ its target is zero, and for $p>0$ its source is zero. Hence all homotopies are zero, so this is a bijection on homotopy classes as well. The homotopy formula used here is the one in [def-pur-kinjective-complex].

source.place: Tag 06XS (lemma-negative-exts), degree-zero endpoint calculation, made explicit with a nonnegative injective resolution

proof.text: Let $p:P\to H^0(P)[0]$ be $\pi$ in degree zero and zero elsewhere. Step 5 constructs precisely $f=s\circ u[0]\circ p$. Under step 4 its class is $u[0]\circ Qp\circ(Qe)^{-1}$, which is precomposition with the canonical truncation $t_E:E\to\mathcal H^0(E)[0]$. This proves that the requested canonical map itself is bijective. Taking $H^0$ of this expression gives $u$, since $H^0(t_E)$ is the identity under the truncation identification. Thus its inverse is the map induced by the cohomology functor $H^0$. For any derived morphism $a:E\to E^{\prime}$ and module morphism $b:M\to M^{\prime}$, functoriality gives $H^0(b[0]\circ v\circ a)=b\circ H^0(v)\circ H^0(a)$. Since the inverse bijections are $H^0$, this identity proves naturality in both variables and independence of all choices of representatives and resolutions.

split_report.summary: Proved both clauses by a nonpositive good truncation and a nonnegative bounded-below injective resolution. Reused all resolution, Grothendieck, truncation and localization lemmas; created no new nodes. Wrote the two degree-zero chain conditions and vanishing of every possible homotopy, identified the resulting bijection with the canonical truncation map, and proved naturality on arbitrary derived morphisms by H^0. The statement is unchanged.

Step 3: def-pur-derived-internal-hom explicitly allows any K-injective target and any source representative. For n<0 every term ∏Hom(P^p,I^{p+n}) is zero, since P^p=0 for p>0 and I^{p+n}=0 for p≤0. Step 4: kinjective-hom-derived holds for every source N, so P need not be bounded below. Step 5: I checked the components by hand. Only f^0 can be nonzero, its chain conditions are d_I^0f^0=0 and f^0d_P^{-1}=0, and every homotopy is zero; so Hom_K(P,I)=Hom(H^0P,M). Step 6: p is a chain map, the class of s∘u[0]∘p is u[0]∘t_E, and H^0 is the inverse, which gives naturality for arbitrary derived morphisms.
